chapters.html:
Understand what PV Info does, choose your starting point and complete a useful first session.

What PV Info helps you do

PV Info brings public pharmacovigilance updates, research, company product evidence and regulatory source documents into a shared reading and review environment. It also supports private company assessments, assigned actions and recorded closure. An automatically matched item is a review prompt; it is not a conclusion that a requirement applies to your company.

Your first ten minutes

  1. Open Updates and select a country or body, a topic and a publication window.
  2. Open an update's original source. Check its publication date, jurisdiction and authority before relying on its summary.
  3. Open Company Explorer and find a company, brand or substance. Inspect Sources & coverage so you understand the limits of the portfolio.
  4. Explore Substances for ingredient/product relationships, Label Intelligence for captured wording changes, or Safety Topics for cross-source evidence. Open Research to explore papers and the innovation timeline, or Source Documents to inspect regulatory evidence.
  5. If you need a saved company workspace, create an account, choose a user ID and password, and check your approval status. Public browsing remains available while approval is pending.
  6. After approval, configure My Company Briefing, confirm products and markets, then use the Company Change Inbox and Action Center.

Understand access before saving

Access stateWhat to expect
Not signed inPublic reading and discovery. Some existing tools offer browser-only workspace features. These are not a private cloud account or a shared team record.
Signed in, approval pendingPublic modules remain accessible. View private approval status and administrator messages. Personal company profiles, assessment saves and team work remain locked until approval.
Approved accountSave supported personal work and use authorized team workflows. Select the intended privacy scope before saving.
Site administratorAdditional account, source, content and refresh controls; access is checked by the server. A professional-role preference does not grant administrator rights.

Navigation and guide conventions

Menus are grouped by default into Updates, My Briefing, Explore and Resources. Administrators can rename groups, move items and hide optional links. The page names and direct links in this guide remain useful when your menu labels differ. Controls that depend on a selected record may appear only after you select it. A hidden menu entry does not replace access control.

This guide describes the implemented application, not proposed backlog features. It was reviewed against the Leadership Cockpit release, including Drug Name Resolver, Substance Explorer, Label Intelligence and Safety Topic Explorer on 3 November 2026. Actual data coverage and review status are shown inside the app. The guide is not evidence that the application is validated for a regulated intended use.

Keep work appropriate for this app

Use organizational descriptions. Do not enter patient narratives, dates of birth, personal addresses, phone/fax numbers or credentials into searches, public annotations, requirement text, evidence links or support messages. Where a workflow explicitly requests an owner/reviewer email, enter only the authorized work identifier. Never publish passwords, recovery keys, temporary passwords or private assessment exports in GitHub issues.

Use notice and AI disclosure

Read the full use, validation and trademark notice, also linked from the site footer. PV Info was built using AI assistance including Claude and ChatGPT; content and outputs may contain inaccuracies. Qualified human review is mandatory before relying on, sharing or implementing results. The Sandbox, E2B Studio and Configuration Workbench are independent training and planning aids, not regulatory submission tools. Their relevant exports carry a versioned copy of the notice. Third-party materials require the applicable rights and permissions.

chapters.title: Accounts, approval and recovery
chapters.summary: Create a user-ID account, understand approval, maintain access and recover a password without relying on email.
chapters.html:
Create a user-ID account, understand approval, maintain access and recover a password without relying on email.

Create an account without email

  1. Open Create your PV Info account.
  2. Choose a unique user ID rather than your legal name. Follow the format validation shown by the form.
  3. Choose and confirm your own password. Use the form's password requirements; the current password setup expects a strong password of at least 12 characters. Use Show password only in a private setting.
  4. Optionally select a professional role. It personalizes context; it does not authorize editing or administration.
  5. Select Create my account and read the resulting approval information.
  6. Save the recovery key securely when it is offered. Treat it like a password and keep it outside the app in an appropriate password manager.

You do not need to submit a name, date of birth, phone number or public contact address for this flow. Do not create a second account to fix a password problem with an existing one.

Sign in and check approval

Open Account and team, enter your user ID and password, and select Sign in securely. A pending user can browse public content and open Approval status & messages. This page checks status and administrator messages while it remains visible; Check for updates requests another check.

Approval unlocks the personal company workspace and other authorized saves. If approval is recorded but the app still shows pending access, sign out and sign in once to refresh the session. If access was declined, read the administrator's explanation; Request reconsideration is available when applicable. Approval is not communicated by a guaranteed email notification.

Account preferences and passwords

In Account and team, use Save account preferences for supported user-ID/professional-role preferences. Set or change password requires entering and confirming a new password. Signing out ends the current app session; it does not erase browser-only data or revoke copies of exported files. The header intentionally does not display your name or email.

An administrator-provisioned account follows a different first-sign-in path: enter the supplied temporary credentials, choose a permanent password when prompted, then sign in with it. Temporary credentials expire and are not a shared default password.

Recover a forgotten password

  1. Open Account and team and expand Forgot password? Use your recovery key.
  2. Enter your user ID, the recovery key and a new permanent password.
  3. Select Reset password using a key and follow the confirmation before signing in again.
  4. An older, unused recovery code may also be accepted for an existing account. Do not assume every historical code remains valid.

Generate or replace recovery key invalidates earlier keys/codes. Copy the new secret when shown; it is not a message to the administrator. The UI clears displayed secrets when appropriate, so do not depend on retrieving them later.

If you lost both password and key

Use Request administrator assistance on the account page. This records a support request; it does not prove ownership, reveal a password or automatically issue a reset. An administrator must handle identity verification through an appropriate process. A public user-ID request by itself must not transfer an account to someone else.

Existing email sign-in

Sign in by email instead remains available for existing email-backed accounts when configured. Request one link, use the newest message and wait if a rate limit appears. Repeated requests can worsen the limit. New user-ID accounts do not need this email path. The approval-status messages and password/key flow do not depend on email delivery.

Teams

Approved users can create or join a team through Account and team. Use only an invitation from the intended team owner and confirm the selected team before saving work. Team membership determines who can see that team's work. See My PV Briefing and teams and Action Center for the difference between personal and team records.

chapters.title: Updates, search and global discovery
chapters.summary: Find updates, understand impact cards and explore the same evidence through country views, the archive and Ask PV Info.
chapters.html:
Find updates, understand impact cards and explore the same evidence through country views, the archive and Ask PV Info.

Find and filter updates

  1. Open Updates.
  2. Enter a medicine, safety topic, agency or phrase in Search. Start broad, then narrow the country/body and topic.
  3. Choose Regulators for official feeds, News for secondary reporting, or All for both. An Official badge describes the source classification, not a company-applicability decision.
  4. Select Published within. The homepage windows cover recent content; use Archive for older collected records.
  5. Use Follow this country and Only countries I follow to focus on followed countries. Following is a reading preference, not a statement that you operate in that market.
  6. Select Clear filters if results look unexpectedly empty. Show more reveals another page of matching results.

Filtered views can be represented in the page URL. Share only the public reading link; do not append confidential product plans or patient details to a search URL. Dates without source evidence must not be interpreted as known effective dates.

Read an update and its impact card

Open the original-source title link to inspect the notice. Impact card expands the app's structured reading prompts: what may have changed, possible business/technical implications, source-stated dates and supporting terms. Classification and potential impacts are produced by rules and may be incomplete or wrong. They are not a legal interpretation or an approved implementation requirement.

Supported save, assess, assign, follow and dismiss actions depend on account state and the current workspace. Add a reason where requested. Saving an item does not create a verified company case automatically. For the full company workflow, confirm products/markets in Company Briefing and continue through the Inbox and Action Center.

Key updates and empty results

Key updates this week prioritizes recent matching items; it is not a guarantee that every important notice was captured. An empty result means no loaded records matched your filters. It does not mean the agency issued no notices or that your company has no obligation. Clear filters, widen the date range, inspect the original regulator site and ask an administrator about missing coverage if necessary.

Ask PV Info

Open the chat bubble and try an organizational query such as FDA safety alerts this week or nitrosamine recalls. Ask PV Info searches the app's loaded update index and returns source-linked matches. It does not provide a general legal/medical answer or retrieve every document on the web. It is not an administrator support inbox; messages are not guaranteed to reach an administrator. Use the account assistance route for access problems.

Global view and regulator directory

Global view presents updates geographically. Select a country or an international-body marker to inspect its recent updates. Map intensity and safety/recall indicators reflect collected records, not country-level risk or completeness.

Regulators helps you find agencies and public source links. Sources we cover describes configured feed coverage. A country appearing in a directory is not proof that all of its primary documents are ingested, translated or verified.

Search the Archive

Open Archive, choose search words, country, topic, official/news scope and From/To dates, then Search. Clear resets the criteria and Show more loads additional matching records. The archive contains previously collected updates, not a complete historical regulator archive. Public reading does not require signing in when the service is available.

Follow RSS

The RSS feed provides recent public updates to a compatible reader. It is separate from private company assessment status. RSS can serve the last built copy during a runtime-data outage, so compare publication/retrieval evidence rather than assuming every fetch represents a newly collected item.

chapters.title: My PV Briefing, workspace and teams
chapters.summary: Tailor your reading view, maintain saved work, and distinguish local, personal and shared records.
chapters.html:
Tailor your reading view, maintain saved work, and distinguish local, personal and shared records.

Build a reading profile

  1. Open My PV Briefing.
  2. Use the introductory profile flow or Edit profile to select the view you read for, countries, topics and watchlist terms.
  3. Select Show my briefing or Save profile. Skip and show everything is useful when you are exploring before choosing a scope.
  4. Choose Last 24 hours, Since my last visit, Last 7 days or Last 30 days.
  5. Review New on what you follow, More in your scope, Coming up and My work. These are different presentations of available evidence and workspace records, not separate source collections.

The reading profile is distinct from a confirmed company portfolio. Selecting a safety-systems role or a watchlist term does not select the company's products and markets for an assessment.

Organize groups

Groups lets you rename or add reading views. Use Add a group, edit the supported labels/preferences, then Save groups. Cancel discards unsaved group edits. Group names are personal organization aids; they do not create access-control roles, operating procedures or regulatory approvals.

Save and review work

Open an impact card, save it, or record the supported assessment/dismissal action with a reason. My work brings saved and pending items back into view. Changes to source content do not by themselves close your work. For assigned actions and verified closure, use the separate Action Center case workflow.

Understand where data is stored

ScopeStorage and sharing behavior
This browser onlyLocal browser storage. It can be lost if site data is cleared, a different browser is used or storage is unavailable. It is not a cross-device or independently verified team record.
Approved personal accountSupported account/workspace records are saved under the signed-in account. Other ordinary users cannot browse your personal company work merely by selecting the same public company.
Selected teamTeam-authorized records are visible to the team's members. A company name alone does not define team access.

Signing in does not mean every type of local object has automatically become a team record. Check the active scope on each workflow. Explicitly select the intended team rather than assuming the last-used team is correct.

Create and join teams

Use Account and team to create a team or join with an invitation. Follow the displayed team controls for available invitation and membership operations. Protect invitation codes and share them only with intended participants. A member's professional-role text is not proof of regulated-role qualification.

Team queue shows the shared update assessments/assignments and activity available to the selected team. It is related to, but not interchangeable with, the company Action Center. Use the Action Center when you need the full company applicability, owner, evidence and closure record.

Export and import

Export workspace (JSON) creates a portable snapshot of supported briefing/workspace data. Import workspace loads a compatible exported snapshot; read any confirmation and check the resulting profile/items. Export assessments (CSV) provides the supported assessment view for analysis.

These exports are not guaranteed to include every cloud case, team membership, source original or database audit event. Use Export this private case for an Action Center case package. Keep downloads in an approved location and inspect them before sharing; they may include organizational work and authorized email identifiers.

Verify a save

Look for the success message, reload the relevant screen and confirm the item appears in the intended scope. If a conflict or sync error is shown, keep your unsaved text and resolve it before assuming a cloud save succeeded. Browser-only evidence is useful for exploration but should not be represented as an independently approved regulated record.

chapters.title: Company Explorer and Portfolio 360
chapters.summary: Explore marketed products, study medicines, therapeutic areas and source coverage before confirming a private company scope.
chapters.html:
Explore marketed products, study medicines, therapeutic areas and source coverage before confirming a private company scope.

Find the correct company

Open Company Explorer. Search by company name, alias, brand or substance; narrow the available browse/type filters. Check legal names, former names, parent/subsidiary information and disambiguation notes before choosing a result. Similar company names are not necessarily the same legal entity.

Following a company is a reading preference. Visiting a public company page does not publish your private selected portfolio or reveal which other users follow it.

Use the company tabs

TabWhat it shows and how to use it
OverviewProfile, evidence coverage and summary context. Read provisional/draft notices.
Portfolio 360Public clinical-study evidence, conditions/therapeutic groupings, study phases and medicines.
Related updatesUpdates matched by company/product/substance/class context. Inspect why each match was made.
Products & marketsSource-linked product records, market, authorization number, holder, ingredient and status.
ResearchRelated papers with maturity and match context.
Sources & coverageSource provenance, last good collection and explicit coverage gaps.

Explore marketed products

Use Search products for a brand, substance or authorization number. Filter the available markets and statuses. A discontinued or withdrawn source record is not the same as a currently marketed medicine. Holder names and company mappings can require review, especially after mergers or licensing changes.

Current product mapping relies principally on the configured FDA Orange Book and EMA medicines sources. Do not infer complete worldwide product coverage, all US biologics/vaccines, every national authorization or all licensing relationships. Missing products may reflect a coverage or mapping gap rather than true absence.

Find clinical trials and investigational medicines

  1. Open Portfolio 360.
  2. Search by NCT ID, study medicine or condition.
  3. Combine Trial phase, Trial status, Therapeutic area / condition group, Study country and Company trial relationship filters. More filters exposes additional options when collapsed.
  4. Distinguish Lead sponsor from Collaborator. The same company can have different reported roles across studies.
  5. Inspect study medicines and experimental-arm evidence. Open the official trial record to verify status, dates, intervention details and organization relationships.
  6. Load more registry pages when available. Reset clinical filters if a loaded subset has no matches.

Therapeutic areas are groupings from condition evidence. They are not a medically validated disease ontology or proof of a company's commercial franchise. Study medicines do not establish ownership, approval, active development rights or inclusion in a company's marketed portfolio. Phases may overlap in study records, so phase counts are not a count of unique products.

Read collection indicators

Complete, partial, not checked, source unavailable and mapping-outdated states describe collection/mapping evidence. A partial result can preserve the prior usable portfolio while a refresh is unfinished. Review retrieval dates and source status before relying on a study's current status. No loaded results is not a statement that the company has no studies.

Prepare a company briefing

Select Build my company briefing to confirm the company, product records and markets in the next workflow. You still make the scope decision; exploring Portfolio 360 does not automatically enroll every study medicine in your confirmed marketed-product profile.

Missing a company? Use the organizational request form in Company Explorer, with a public company website where available. Do not add individual contacts or confidential pipeline information.

chapters.summary: Search ingredients, inspect source-linked holder records and distinguish company relationships from manufacturing evidence.
chapters.html:
Use Explore → Substances to find an active ingredient and inspect the products and companies recorded against it. This public browser does not require sign-in or account approval.

Find an ingredient

  1. Enter an ingredient name, for example paracetamol or acetaminophen.
  2. Select a result. A spelling suggestion is a navigation aid; it does not create a new synonym.
  3. Narrow the directory by market, source, company role, source status or single/combination product. Use the alphabet buttons or clear filters to start again.

The initial reviewed synonym pilot groups paracetamol and acetaminophen. Other ingredient names, including salts and esters, remain distinct unless a reviewed rule explicitly connects them. Original ingredient strings remain visible on product evidence.

Review the evidence

The ingredient page has four views:

  • Overview: identity approach, source-record counts and coverage limitations.
  • Companies: entities named in the source, their recorded roles and linked product evidence. Optional corporate grouping uses existing curated company mappings; it does not prove legal identity or manufacturing.
  • Products: source-level product records, ingredient combinations, strengths/forms as supplied, source status and original links. FDA presentation numbers distinguish presentations; EMA authorization records may not supply individual presentations.
  • Sources: capture dates, source coverage and reviewed naming evidence.

An FDA application holder or EMA marketing authorization holder is not automatically a manufacturer. The initial datasets do not establish API manufacturers or manufacturing sites. Selecting the manufacturer filter can return no records; this means manufacturing evidence is unavailable, not that no manufacturers exist. An unmapped holder is still shown even when no curated Company Explorer profile exists.

Continue company work

Open a linked company profile to inspect its wider portfolio. A briefing link can preselect a company, but you must confirm your own products and markets before private assessment. Browsing an ingredient does not create or alter your private company profile.

Counts describe records in the captured FDA Orange Book and EMA medicine datasets, not all global products, suppliers or currently marketed stock. Source status does not establish present commercial availability. Refer to the source dates and official record before relying on a relationship.

Naming rules are versioned editorial configuration in the repository for this release. Changes require reviewed evidence and a code review; there is no automatic fuzzy-name merge or public alias editing. Clinical medicines, global API supplier discovery and substance-specific signal interpretation are outside this initial release.

Related review workflows

Use Label Intelligence for captured safety wording and Safety Topic Explorer for topic evidence across labels, updates and research. Select Resolve a medicine name in the directory or ingredient page. The Drug Name Resolver uses US-focused RxNorm candidates and structured source details; it does not silently merge ingredient identities. chapters.summary: Review company priorities, product and market impact, assigned dates, coverage and management snapshots across separate personal and team scopes.
chapters.html:
Open your company view

Open My Briefing → PV Control Tower, or use the Control Tower link on My Briefing, Company Briefing or Action Center. First confirm products and markets in Company Briefing. Each company has its own monitoring scope.

Select a company and a work visibility scope. My private account, Team, and This browser only are separate views. Account work uses existing access controls; selecting a company does not grant access to other users' cases. Browser-only work is visible to anyone using the same browser profile. Pending accounts need approval for company work.

Review what needs attention

The summary cards open filtered priority lists: overdue actions, actions due within seven days, awaiting assessment, awaiting verification, and evidence without a linked case in the selected scope. Priorities show recorded owners, assigned due dates and links to original evidence and existing cases.

Work comes from Action Center. Evidence candidates come from confirmed-product company update and research matches over the last 365 days and captured label changes. Missing dates can appear and do not mean that evidence is new. A source match is not a decision on applicability. Existing cases, including closed cases, suppress duplicate new-case prompts; this does not establish that a later source revision has been assessed. Review changed evidence through Company Inbox.

Focus products and markets

Use the market and product filters or Focus product in Products × markets. Product counts can overlap because an item can concern multiple products. Case context is the frozen product scope recorded when the assessment began; it can differ from today's portfolio. Company-wide cases without product details appear in the all-product view.

Review areas are keyword prompts for evidence without a linked case. They are not assignments, responsibility determinations or notifications. Assigned action dates are internal recorded dates, not automatically calculated statutory reporting deadlines.

Continue the work

Continue in Action Center opens the existing case in its original scope. In browser-only mode, new evidence opens Company Briefing for a local assessment handoff. Signed-in private and team evidence opens Company Inbox; label evidence opens Label Intelligence. No new cases, assignments or decisions are created automatically.

Use Refresh after another tab changes work or portfolio scope. Reconfirm changed product records before loading new priorities. Signing out, changing accounts or losing approval clears the current private dashboard. Do not rely on a downloaded snapshot after access or source evidence changes.

Download and interpret a snapshot

Download management snapshot saves a JSON file for the current company, market, product and visibility scope. It includes loaded-at time, portfolio revision, priorities, product counts, recorded dates and explicit coverage limitations. Keep private downloads under your company's document controls.

If cases cannot load completely, work metrics and evidence-to-case linkage are unavailable, not zero. If labels cannot load, other evidence remains available with a coverage gap. The coverage panel separates company confirmation, source capture dates and the current dashboard load time.

The Control Tower is not a compliance attestation or a validated regulatory record. It does not automatically aggregate every country requirement, clinical-study change, product licence, partner agreement or statutory deadline. Leadership Cockpit offers topic watches and a weekly brief; Company Inbox includes additional regulatory and clinical evidence. Qualified human review is mandatory.

chapters.title: Confirm My Company Briefing
chapters.summary: Select a company, confirm products and markets, then hand relevant evidence to assessment.
chapters.html:
Select a company, confirm products and markets, then hand relevant evidence to assessment.

Before you start

Use an approved account to save a private company profile. Public company evidence remains browseable without approval. Decide whether you are setting up a personal workspace or a selected team's work. Use real organizational scope only where you are authorized to maintain it.

Confirm products and markets

  1. Open My Company Briefing.
  2. Search Company name or alias and choose the correct result.
  3. Read the company's coverage and product-mapping limitations.
  4. Select the markets you need to monitor.
  5. Select the supported product records relevant to that scope. Verify source, ingredient and authorization identifiers rather than relying only on brand text.
  6. Select Confirm scope and build briefing.
  7. Check that the displayed company, market and product selections match your intention.

A confirmed profile records your selection and its revision/confirmation context. It is not a declaration that public source coverage is complete. The current product selection is based on the records the app can verify; do not assume unlisted investigational medicines are automatically covered.

Read the matched briefing

Updates to review and Research to explore are organized around your confirmed scope. Read the source, publication date, match reason and affected market. A direct product match is more specific than a substance, class, corporate or jurisdiction association, but none replaces an applicability decision.

Review outside-market notices deliberately. A foreign source can be useful for signal monitoring without imposing the same local legal obligation. The app may require an explicit outside-market confirmation before an assessment handoff.

Send an item for assessment

  1. Open its source evidence and review why it matched.
  2. Select Send for assessment where available.
  3. Confirm the intended work scope/destination.
  4. Read the saved/under-assessment confirmation.
  5. Continue in Action Center; a briefing handoff is not a completed applicability decision or assigned action.

An existing handoff should be continued rather than recreated. Reading, saving, starting assessment and verified closure are different states. The Company Change Inbox helps you keep those states separate.

Keep the scope current

When source product records or mappings change, the app can require reconfirmation before new assessments. Reopen Company Briefing, inspect the changed portfolio, reselect/confirm the intended products and markets, then reload the inbox. Existing cases retain their pinned evidence and portfolio context; a new public product does not silently rewrite an old case.

Automated source refresh can add or update public products/studies. It does not mean every new medicine is automatically selected into your confirmed private profile, or that a new study has been classified as company-applicable.

Privacy

Many users can browse J&J, GSK, AstraZeneca or any other public company without exposing their personal selection to one another. Public company pages are shared reference evidence. A personal profile, reading history and company case remain within the applicable account/team controls. Team work is intentionally shared with authorized members. Review the chosen scope before exporting or sharing.

Triage new evidence and continue company work without confusing reading status with assessment status.

Open your company inbox

  1. Confirm a company, products and markets in Company Briefing.
  2. Open My Company Change Inbox.
  3. Choose Confirmed company and Work privacy scope.
  4. Select Reload inbox after a portfolio change, source refresh or action taken elsewhere.

If the screen asks you to reconfirm a changed portfolio, return to Company Briefing first. Do not assume the app's previous product selection still represents the latest source records.

Filter the evidence queue

Search evidence narrows available items. Evidence type separates product updates, research, regulatory source reviews, clinical studies and label changes. Reading state offers Unread & updated, All reading states, Seen and Updated since seen. Reset filters returns to the default view and Show next 30 reveals further items.

The evidence queue contains what matched available company context. It is not an exhaustive list of every publication or every company obligation. Clinical evidence and regulator-wide reviews may have broader matching logic than a directly identified product.

Read, mark and assess

Control/stateMeaning
Mark as seenRecords that you reviewed this evidence version in the current scope. It does not approve applicability.
Mark unreadReturns it to your reading queue; it does not reopen a closed case.
Updated since seenThe evidence fingerprint changed after the recorded reading marker. Recheck it.
Start assessmentOpens the appropriate company assessment when evidence and permissions are ready.
Continue assessmentOpens the existing linked case rather than creating parallel work.
View verified closureOpens the existing completed case; inspect its decision/evidence rather than inferring a new assessment.
Review company trialsTakes you to clinical evidence. A study row is not automatically a regulatory action case.

For a regulatory source review awaiting human triage, Start assessment is locked or replaced by a source-review route. Use Regulatory Change Review to compare and triage it first. Matching alone must not turn an unconfirmed text change into a company obligation.

Inbox answers: what is new, what have I read, and is there existing work? Action Center answers: does it apply, what action is assigned, and has closure been verified? Starting a case from Inbox carries the original evidence and company context forward. Opening the same item again should take you to that case, not create another decision trail.

Your open work summarizes awaiting assessment, actions due, overdue and awaiting verification for the selected company/scope. Switch to the intended personal account or team before interpreting those counts.

If reading status cannot be saved, retry before assuming the marker persisted. If assessment status cannot load, do not create a duplicate to bypass the error. Reload the inbox, check sign-in/approval, then continue the existing case. If no items appear, clear the reading-state filter and verify both the company scope and source coverage.

Substance Explorer provides public ingredient/product evidence; your private scope still requires Company Briefing confirmation.

Leadership Cockpit and Company Safety Watch summarizes the same evidence and case records. A focused Inbox link preserves the selected confirmed company, authorized team and exact evidence key; All reading states is selected so a previously seen item remains reachable. chapters.summary: Find official source documents, inspect captured versions and reach extraction and baseline review.
chapters.html:
Find official source documents, inspect captured versions and reach extraction and baseline review.

Find a document

Open Source Documents. Combine Search documents, country/jurisdiction, agency, topic, lifecycle and document type. Use Published from/through for stated source publication dates and Monitoring for active/inactive collection configuration.

Select a result to inspect the source title, issuing agency, classification, source dates and latest capture evidence. Official primary source identifies the provenance category. It does not prove that the parser captured every clause or that the source's legal force was correctly interpreted.

Inspect captured versions

  1. Use Captured document version to choose a version rather than assuming the latest is the one relevant to your case.
  2. Open agency source for the regulator's current publication.
  3. Use Download archived original where available to inspect the captured original. Its bytes may differ from the current official URL after a revision.
  4. Read Evidence checksum & method, retrieval/capture details and capture status.
  5. Use View linked baseline requirements to find interpretations derived from that source family.

The original hash identifies captured bytes; the content hash/parser information describes extraction. Reprocessing unchanged bytes with an improved parser is not proof of a regulatory amendment. Source publication date, effective date and retrieval date are separate facts.

Understand capture and extraction states

Not captured means the record is registered but no usable capture is present. Metadata-only means you have a reference record without extracted document text. Partial/unsupported extraction requires manual review. An unchanged byte comparison can preserve a prior capture or reprocess extraction without inventing a new legal change.

Extraction candidate view filters candidates such as Awaiting review, Potential changes, Unchanged text and Accepted into baseline library. Open a candidate to inspect its source anchor, quoted text, context, prior match and comparison. Link to this exact candidate is a provenance link, not an approval.

Review automatic drafts

Review automatic baseline drafts opens the admin-only Baseline Review desk for the captured document. Automatic preparation reduces retyping; it does not certify completeness. A source can contain tables, cross-references, exceptions, scanned content and non-normative material that need human examination.

The older Match & draft baseline candidate route also exists for explicit matching to a stable requirement. Use it deliberately when a candidate must be linked to an existing obligation; do not create a parallel stable ID for the same meaning. Reject candidate and Need more information record a rationale. Such organizational editorial notes are public-facing record content, so exclude confidential company decisions and personal details.

Administrator: register or edit a source

  1. Select Register an official document, or Edit monitored source for an existing record.
  2. Choose a verified agency and matching jurisdiction. Use the official source URL and a stable source-family ID.
  3. Complete title/edition, topic, lifecycle, authority metadata, legal basis/applicability context, dates when known and capture frequency/monitoring status.
  4. Leave unknown dates unknown; do not substitute retrieval time as publication/effective date.
  5. Select Save document source. Automatic collection/extraction is scheduled; Capture now requests an immediate supported capture when available.
  6. Revisit the captured version and Baseline Review. Saving a source does not publish its extracted drafts.

Only approved agency domains and supported official URLs can be captured. An access-denied landing page, unsupported PDF or scanned source may need editorial intervention rather than repeated capture requests.

Agency directory and coverage gaps

Global agency directory & coverage gaps shows supported agency records and verification state. Administrators can register/edit an agency, its country, official website and allowed domains, recording verification evidence. A listed but unverified agency is not an active verified capture policy. Coverage gaps should remain visible; missing extracted requirements do not mean the jurisdiction has no requirements.

Source Documents and provenance

Find official source documents, inspect captured versions and reach extraction and baseline review.

 Find a document
Open Source Documents. Combine Search documents, country/jurisdiction, agency, topic, lifecycle and document type. Use Published from/through for stated source publication dates and Monitoring for active/inactive collection configuration.

Select a result to inspect the source title, issuing agency, classification, source dates and latest capture evidence. Official primary source identifies the provenance category. It does not prove that the parser captured every clause or that the source's legal force was correctly interpreted.

 Inspect captured versions
1. Use Captured document version to choose a version rather than assuming the latest is the one relevant to your case.
2. Open agency source for the regulator's current publication.
3. Use Download archived original where available to inspect the captured original. Its bytes may differ from the current official URL after a revision.
4. Read Evidence checksum & method, retrieval/capture details and capture status.
5. Use View linked baseline requirements to find interpretations derived from that source family.

The original hash identifies captured bytes; the content hash/parser information describes extraction. Reprocessing unchanged bytes with an improved parser is not proof of a regulatory amendment. Source publication date, effective date and retrieval date are separate facts.

 Understand capture and extraction states
Not captured means the record is registered but no usable capture is present. Metadata-only means you have a reference record without extracted document text. Partial/unsupported extraction requires manual review. An unchanged byte comparison can preserve a prior capture or reprocess extraction without inventing a new legal change.

Extraction candidate view filters candidates such as Awaiting review, Potential changes, Unchanged text and Accepted into baseline library. Open a candidate to inspect its source anchor, quoted text, context, prior match and comparison. Link to this exact candidate is a provenance link, not an approval.

 Review automatic drafts
Review automatic baseline drafts opens the admin-only Baseline Review desk for the captured document. Automatic preparation reduces retyping; it does not certify completeness. A source can contain tables, cross-references, exceptions, scanned content and non-normative material that need human examination.

The older Match & draft baseline candidate route also exists for explicit matching to a stable requirement. Use it deliberately when a candidate must be linked to an existing obligation; do not create a parallel stable ID for the same meaning. Reject candidate and Need more information record a rationale. Such organizational editorial notes are public-facing record content, so exclude confidential company decisions and personal details.

 Administrator: register or edit a source
1. Select Register an official document, or Edit monitored source for an existing record.
2. Choose a verified agency and matching jurisdiction. Use the official source URL and a stable source-family ID.
3. Complete title/edition, topic, lifecycle, authority metadata, legal basis/applicability context, dates when known and capture frequency/monitoring status.
4. Leave unknown dates unknown; do not substitute retrieval time as publication/effective date.
5. Select Save document source. Automatic collection/extraction is scheduled; Capture now requests an immediate supported capture when available.
6. Revisit the captured version and Baseline Review. Saving a source does not publish its extracted drafts.

Only approved agency domains and supported official URLs can be captured. An access-denied landing page, unsupported PDF or scanned source may need editorial intervention rather than repeated capture requests.

 Agency directory and coverage gaps
Global agency directory & coverage gaps shows supported agency records and verification state. Administrators can register/edit an agency, its country, official website and allowed domains, recording verification evidence. A listed but unverified agency is not an active verified capture policy. Coverage gaps should remain visible; missing extracted requirements do not mean the jurisdiction has no requirements.

chapters.title: Baseline Review: draft to publication
chapters.summary: Review automatically prepared requirements against the original document before publishing a human-reviewed version.
chapters.html:
Review automatically prepared requirements against the original document before publishing a human-reviewed version.

Access the review desk

Sign in with an approved site-administrator account. From Source Documents select the source/capture and Review automatic baseline drafts. You can also open Baseline Review directly. The current review desk is administrator-controlled; the app does not yet expose every proposed specialist role as a separate permission tier.

Choose Captured document, filter Stage and use Find a clause. The desk prepares supported drafts automatically from the selected capture. Draft count and capture/coverage messages describe available extraction output, not a certification that every regulatory requirement was found.

Review a draft

  1. Select a draft in the list.
  2. Read Captured source evidence, its context, citation/anchor and parser/capture status.
  3. Open official source and Open archived document. Review the surrounding sections, definitions, tables, exceptions and referenced documents.
  4. Check Title, Statement, Authority type, Legal basis, Applicability and Exceptions. A guidance source should not become binding law merely because a sentence uses an imperative word.
  5. Expand Source metadata, dates and implementation prompts. Check lifecycle, source status, effective/publication dates, systems/process prompts and change rationale. Locked provenance fields identify the source and must not be casually rewritten.
  6. Select Save draft before taking a workflow action.

Record missing information honestly. System prompts are generic assessment aids; they do not establish how Argus Safety, Veeva Safety, ARISg or a company's customized process must change.

Move through the actual lifecycle

StageAvailable next actions
DraftSave draft; Submit for review; Reject draft.
In reviewReturn to draft; Publish reviewed requirement; Reject draft.
PublishedOpen the published requirement and its history. Use Requirements Library for subsequent revisions.
RejectedRetained decision state; it is not an approved baseline obligation.

Unsaved edits must be saved before submission/publication. Changing selection while editing can ask whether to discard unsaved changes. If another reviewer changes the record, reload and compare before retrying; do not overwrite a newer revision blindly.

Publish a reviewed requirement

  1. In the in-review draft, enter a clear Decision rationale.
  2. Choose a Stable requirement ID for a new obligation. Keep it stable across later revisions of the same underlying meaning.
  3. If that stable ID already exists, stop and revise the existing obligation in Requirements Library. The desk intentionally blocks parallel IDs that could duplicate an approved baseline.
  4. Confirm Source evidence reviewed only after checking the full source, wording, authority, applicability, conditions, dates and extraction coverage.
  5. Select Publish reviewed requirement and inspect the success message.
  6. Select Open published requirement and verify its source/version/status in Requirements Library.

Publication is a human-reviewed library decision. Company applicability remains undecided. The current admin workflow does not justify claiming independent dual approval, a validated electronic signature or GxP compliance where those controls have not been implemented and qualified.

History and omissions

Draft decision history records supported commands, revisions, rationale and times. A previously accepted/rejected candidate is not necessarily redrafted automatically. If no draft appears, inspect the extraction candidate view and the original document; absence can represent prior disposition, unsupported extraction or a coverage gap. Do not repeatedly import duplicates to make the count look complete.

When a source revision arrives, preserve the older source and requirement history, compare evidence and create a reviewed successor interpretation where warranted. Automatic extraction must not overwrite a published baseline merely because new text was detected.

chapters.title: Requirements Library and baseline releases
chapters.summary: Explore source-linked interpretations, distinguish current evidence from approved baselines and assess a pinned version for your company.
chapters.html:
Explore source-linked interpretations, distinguish current evidence from approved baselines and assess a pinned version for your company.

Choose the workspace

Open Requirements Library. The workspace includes Requirements explorer, Baseline releases, Research intake, Coverage map and Company workflow. Start with the view that matches your task rather than treating every visible row as an approved legal obligation.

Search and filter interpretations

Use Search, Country/jurisdiction, Agency, Topic and Lifecycle. View distinguishes Latest captures, Awaiting review, Approved baseline on date and Approved upcoming. Applies on is the date the requirement is assessed as effective; Known/approved by restricts what review evidence was available by the selected date.

A latest capture can be unapproved. Approved baseline views exclude undated or unapproved interpretations and apply version/date rules. An unknown start date must not be guessed. The applicable successor is considered before an expired/withdrawn version so an old obligation is not silently resurrected.

Inspect one requirement

  1. Select a requirement and note its stable key and revision.
  2. Review Source, Edition/clause, Legal basis, publication/effective interval and review status/rationale.
  3. Read Who may be affected, Qualifications & exceptions, Processes to assess, Systems to assess and Historical coverage.
  4. Open the captured source document/extraction history and the official link.
  5. Use Compare with predecessor to review changed captured fields. A field diff is evidence for interpretation, not the official legal text itself.
  6. Inspect earlier versions rather than replacing history with a current summary.

Source register & coverage gaps helps distinguish a registered source from reviewed interpretation coverage. Export shown records exports the current supported view; record the filters and dates when using an export as review evidence.

Master checklist and agency annexes

Common capability controls provide a cross-jurisdiction checklist. The FDA/US, EMA/EU, MHRA/UK, Health Canada and PMDA/MHLW/Japan annex context distinguishes agency-specific obligations and evidence gaps. A common capability is not automatically a legal obligation in all five jurisdictions. Unverified research candidates, especially sources without verified operative text, must remain clearly separate from approved local obligations.

Use agency/control filters to inspect linked items. Follow exact source citations and distinguish regulation, guidance and technical instruction. Do not infer deadlines, responsible parties or submission routes when the operative source has not been verified.

Administrator: revise an interpretation or prepare a release

Use the Library editorial desk to capture a new requirement or revise an existing stable key with a new version. Complete the required source, statement, legal basis, applicability, qualifications, dates and rationale fields. Review/approval actions are separate from a save. Existing approved versions are historical evidence and are not edited in place.

Baseline releases has a Baseline editorial desk and Prepare a release. Review the included approved versions, source relationships, release rationale and the resulting release history. Do not describe a merely prepared or unapproved set as an approved organizational baseline. Inspect the actual status and version set after saving.

Send a version for company assessment

  1. Confirm your portfolio in Company Briefing.
  2. Select the exact requirement version and Assess for my company.
  3. Choose the confirmed Company portfolio and Assessment destination.
  4. If intentionally monitoring a source outside selected markets, read and explicitly confirm that choice.
  5. Select Send this version for assessment, then continue in Action Center.

The handoff pins that requirement version and company context. An approved library interpretation still needs a company applicability decision. If portfolio data changed, reconfirm it before creating a new assessment. A later baseline revision does not silently replace the evidence in an existing case.

chapters.title: Regulatory Change Review
chapters.summary: Compare source captures, record human triage and open a company assessment with pinned evidence.
chapters.html:
Compare source captures, record human triage and open a company assessment with pinned evidence.

Find a source change

Open Regulatory Change Review. Search source reviews, filter agency/jurisdiction/triage status and use Reload register after new captures. Select a change to open its three workflow tabs. An initial capture may have no prior version; missing predecessor evidence must not be interpreted as proof that every clause is new.

1 · Compare evidence

Review Previous capture and Current capture, their source links and version details. Use Show changed sections only to focus on extracted additions/deletions/modifications, then turn it off to inspect context. Show next 40 comparison sections loads more text where available.

Read warnings for partial extraction, changed structure, unsupported/scanned content, missing dates or other uncertainty. Open both original documents where available. A parser change, page relocation or formatting change can produce a text difference without a legal amendment. If comparison is incomplete, record that and perform the necessary manual review rather than declaring no impact.

2 · Human triage

An authorized administrator/editor records the source-level interpretation. The current implemented access check is administrator-based; do not infer a separate regulatory-reviewer permission simply from a professional-role label.

  1. Select Change type.
  2. Enter Reviewer summary describing the source change, not a company implementation conclusion.
  3. Select the Triage decision: a reviewed handoff, more information needed or informational disposition as appropriate to the available choices.
  4. Enter Rationale, scope and uncertainty.
  5. Confirm manual comparison only if you compared the original documents, including relocated text and exceptions.
  6. Select affected approved requirement versions when supported. No selection records an unmapped baseline; it is not proof that no requirements are affected.
  7. Select Save triage decision and inspect the new review revision.

Saving triage does not publish a baseline change automatically. If a new interpretation is needed, use the baseline/library review workflow separately.

3 · Company assessment

After appropriate human triage, use Company assessment:

  1. Choose a confirmed company portfolio.
  2. Choose My private account or an authorized team privacy scope.
  3. Recheck product/market freshness. Explicitly confirm outside-market monitoring only when intended.
  4. Select Open private assessment.
  5. Select Continue in Action Center and decide company applicability there.

The case pins source captures, comparison/triage review and affected requirement evidence. A newer triage review may govern new handoffs while an existing assessment retains the earlier review it actually used. Inspect that pinned context when reopening older work.

Separation of decisions

A source difference answers what text may have changed. Human triage classifies that evidence. The approved baseline records a reviewed interpretation. Company applicability decides whether and how it affects the selected business. Assigned work and verified closure come later. Completing one step does not imply the next has been approved.

chapters.summary: Use the full case workflow, implementation drafts, ownership, evidence and reviewer decisions.
chapters.html:
Use the full case workflow, implementation drafts, ownership, evidence and reviewer decisions.

Open the right case and scope

Open My Company Action Center. Choose Work visibility: This browser only where offered, My private account, or an authorized selected team. Filter by Company, Market, status and Search cases. Refresh loads the latest available cases.

A pending account cannot use protected company saves merely because a public page can be browsed. A browser-only case is local exploratory work and can be lost with browser data. Use an approved personal/team scope for supported persistent workflows.

Assessment handoffs appear separately from existing cases. Select Start case for a handoff, or select an existing case in Cases. Opening the same handoff should continue its record rather than duplicate it.

1 · Review evidence

Read the original source, publication date, why it matched, selected products/markets and pinned portfolio revision. For regulatory cases, open the pinned source comparison/human triage or requirement version. The frozen evidence snapshot records what was used; it does not guarantee the upstream source remains unchanged.

2 · Decide applicability

Choose Relevant, Not relevant or More information needed. Enter Decision reason and Save applicability. Include role/product/lifecycle/jurisdiction qualifications and unresolved questions. More information needed leaves assessment work open.

Reassess applicability clears the current action/completion context. Read the warning and preserve any needed work before changing the decision. A closed case must be reopened with a reason; a case awaiting verification must be returned for rework before changing applicability.

3 · Assign action

For Relevant items, choose Action type, Owner email, Due date and Action instructions, then Save action. Types include label/product information, signal evaluation, risk management, regulatory submission, safety system/process and literature follow-up.

In team work, choose an authorized team member. Enter only the required work email identifier, without a personal name or patient details. Recording an owner is not a guarantee that an email notification was sent, that the person accepted it or that another enterprise task system was updated.

The dashboard shows Awaiting assessment, Actions due, Overdue, Awaiting verification and Closed. Counts follow the current filters/scope. An overdue date is a workflow indicator, not necessarily a verified statutory reporting clock.

Draft business, system, process and data requirements

Where the case exposes implementation drafts, create the appropriate business/system/process/data/training requirement against the case's evidence. Specify the current control, proposed change, rationale, acceptance/verification evidence and the applicable system/process scope using the fields offered. Keep drafts separate from the source text and approved baseline interpretation.

Choose Impact requirement type, then complete statement, acceptance criteria, rationale and system scope. Prepare drafting prompts supplies placeholders that you must replace with reviewed company-specific wording. Save draft (or Save new draft revision) creates a new immutable revision. Enter an Impact draft review note, choose the independent team reviewer when required, and Submit draft for review. The designated reviewer can Approve requirement or Return draft for changes; personal work uses explicit self-review. Export private impact requirements downloads this draft/history package separately from the case export. If applicability changed after drafting, append and review a new revision. Resolve pending/rework items before closure approval. For example, a system requirement should name the affected configuration and expected test outcome without inventing the company's current Argus, Veeva Safety or ARISg setup. A generic library prompt does not know your versions, customizations or operating procedures.

4 · Submit closure evidence

The assigned team owner can submit completion when the workflow requires it. Enter What changed / work performed, a Supporting evidence label and an HTTPS document link. For Not relevant, record Why no action is required with supporting evidence; a reasoned no-action decision still needs the applicable verification step.

Evidence is currently linked by HTTPS URL. Do not assume the app uploads and archives arbitrary attachments. Use a stable organization-approved location that intended reviewers can access. Do not include access tokens, credentials or personal identifiers in URLs. An evidence link alone does not prove its content was independently reviewed.

For team cases, select an independent reviewer who is a different authorized teammate. Personal/local closure is explicitly marked self-reviewed. Select Submit for verification.

5 · Verify or return

The designated team reviewer reviews the submitted work and evidence, enters Reviewer verification note and selects Approve and close. The submitter cannot approve their own team submission through the independent-review route. For a personal case, use Confirm self-review and close and retain the self-review designation.

If evidence is insufficient, enter Rework reason and Return to work. Do not close merely to clear an overdue counter. After closure, Reopen case requires a reason and records another event; it is preferable to pretending a prior decision never existed.

History, export and save conflicts

Case history records supported transitions, versions, actors and timestamps. Export this private case downloads the case JSON; regulatory-change and label-change cases include their supported pinned source evidence packages. Store it securely and inspect completeness for your intended use. It is not automatically a validated e-signature package or a full database audit export.

If the app reports that another tab/user changed the case, your unsaved form is retained where possible. Copy necessary text, Refresh, compare the current version, and retry deliberately. Do not keep clicking Save to bypass concurrency checks.

Start from the right evidence screen

Use Label Intelligence to review an official label source and confirm products before label-case handoff. The source confirmation is not approval of applicability or closure. Reopening the same evidence/company/privacy scope returns the same case; changed source versions retain distinct evidence identities.

Safety Topic Explorer supplies discovery routes to label review, paper details and Company Briefing. It does not automatically create an Action Center case or approve a safety signal. Substance Explorer helps investigate product relationships, while the confirmed company portfolio defines private assessment scope.

Search the research collection

chapters.title: Events, time zones and calendar downloads
chapters.summary: Find source-verified training and events, interpret date-only listings and download calendar files safely.
chapters.html:
Find source-verified training and events, interpret date-only listings and download calendar files safely.

Find an event

Open Events & Training. Use Search, Region, Format and Category. Display time zone changes how supported timed events are displayed. Use month arrows, This month and Month view to browse the calendar; Reset filters clears the selected criteria.

Select an event and inspect organizer, official source, format/location, dates, time information, verification date and status. An agency committee meeting is not automatically open to the public. Follow the official source for attendance eligibility, registration, fees, language and cancellations.

Understand the dates

ListingInterpretation
Confirmed timed eventAn explicit UTC start/end and organizer time zone support conversion to your selected display zone. Check the date as well as the time after conversion.
Date-only listingThe event has civil dates but no verified time. Do not infer midnight, a session duration or a local start time.
Multi-day eventThe source's inclusive dates are shown; the downloaded calendar uses calendar-standard exclusive end boundaries.
Older verificationThe page can warn when verification is aging. Recheck the original source before making attendance plans.

Time-zone conversion does not invent missing source times. The selected display zone is a reading preference, not a change to the organizer's schedule.

Download and import a calendar entry

  1. Open the event and confirm its current official details.
  2. Use its calendar-download control to download the .ics file.
  3. Open/import it in your calendar application and check the date/time zone, duration, title and source link.
  4. For a date-only reminder, read the warning and avoid presenting it as a verified timed appointment.
  5. If facts change, download/import the updated event and check how your calendar client handles its stable event identifier. Remove unintended duplicates through your calendar client's controls.

A downloaded file is a snapshot, not a subscribed live calendar. Changes or cancellations do not automatically update every previously imported calendar. PV Info does not enroll you in an event, submit registration, track attendance or guarantee a reminder from your calendar service.

For curators

The current event collection is curated in the repository, not an unrestricted event-submission/admin editor. Verify facts against the official source, retain stable event IDs, advance verification evidence only after rechecking, increment the calendar sequence when facts change, and preserve cancellation status rather than silently removing a previously published event. No attendee or organizer-contact PII is needed.

Regulatory dates and review

Open Events & Training → Regulatory dates & review, or use the regulatory-dates link on a captured Source Document. This view is separate from meetings and training. Search by source/scope and filter by agency, country, date type, date range and verification. Clear the From date to see historical dates.

Archived document ingestion prepares pending effective-date records from captured metadata. It never substitutes publication dates for deadlines or publishes dates automatically. Identical source bytes do not create duplicate dates when the extractor changes. Different bytes flag a previously verified date as source changed and pause its download until reviewed. Earlier evidence and decision history remain available.

Administrators can open events.html?view=regulatory&review=1 for the pending queue. Open the original and captured evidence, verify the exact date and meaning, specify the page/section, product/reporting scope and timing qualifications, and record a rationale. Verify & publish, reject or withdraw. Reviews enforce a revision check so an outdated screen cannot overwrite a newer decision. Admins can inspect the date's decision history. Company applicability is a separate assessment.

Only verified dates support a date-only .ics download with a stable identifier and increasing sequence. Dates stay on their published civil day. Downloaded reminders are snapshots: later changes do not update a user's calendar automatically. Source-changed or withdrawn records remain visible when their status is selected, but cannot be downloaded as confirmed dates.

Coverage in this release

Automatic intake currently covers effective-date metadata on archived captures, including GVP sources. The date-type model supports compliance, data-lock, submission and consultation dates for review, but EURD spreadsheet ingestion, substance-specific schedule generation, arbitrary PDF deadline extraction and portfolio-matched private milestones are not yet connected. Do not treat this calendar as an exhaustive regulatory schedule. Follow the linked baseline/company workflow to assess an obligation; company work stays in its existing private workspace.

Browse the resource directory

Open Public Safety Data Resources. Search and combine the available category, specialty, jurisdiction/product and access filters. Read What this directory covers and Which resource should I use? before comparing resources.

Open a resource to inspect its organization, purpose, coverage, access/reuse conditions, limitations, official URL and verification/link status. A publicly available reporting database can have duplicates, missingness and reporting bias; its presence in this directory is not a claim that it measures incidence or establishes causality.

Resource directory versus collection

ItemWhat it means
Resource listingA reference to a public database/tool/organization. It can be useful without its records being downloaded into PV Info.
Collected indicatorThe listing is associated with a configured collection source according to the app's current evidence. It does not imply complete ingestion of that database.
Data sourceA configured feed/API/page/news search used by the collection pipeline. Administrators manage this separately.

Suggest or report a resource

Use Suggest a resource for a relevant public organizational reference, or the supported feedback/broken-link controls where available. chapters.title: Admin: accounts and access requests
chapters.summary: Approve signups, communicate privately and handle assistance without shared passwords or automatic identity bypass.
chapters.html:
Approve signups, communicate privately and handle assistance without shared passwords or automatic identity bypass.

Access the module

Sign in with an approved site-administrator account. The Admin menu appears only after administrator authorization is confirmed. Open Admin, then Accounts & access requests. A regular user cannot gain access by choosing a professional role or knowing the URL.

The screen distinguishes self-signup approvals, password assistance, private legacy access requests and advanced temporary-password provisioning. Use Reload requests when checking a newly created account.

Approve a self-signup

  1. Find the requested user ID in Signup approvals. Confirm you are reviewing the intended registration, especially when similar aliases exist.
  2. Follow your organization's approval criteria. Do not infer identity from public profile text alone.
  3. Use the organizational message box when an explanation or instruction is needed.
  4. Select Approve account or Decline signup. Read the success/failure result and reload to confirm the state.
  5. Use Send private message for an account-specific message. Users can read it on Approval status & messages after signing in with their chosen password.

The ordinary self-signup user chooses their own password. Approval does not require an email link, and the app does not guarantee an approval email. Pending users can still navigate public modules; private saved company work remains locked until approval.

If a signup is missing

Check Signup approvals rather than only Private access requests. Reload, confirm the user's exact user ID and inspect whether account creation actually succeeded. Do not create another privileged user or overwrite an existing account as a shortcut. A setup-incomplete/approving state needs investigation before claiming access is granted.

Password assistance

Review the Password assistance requests list and select the appropriate available outcome, such as Identity verification needed, User recovered with a code or Duplicate/no action. Record assistance review documents the review; it does not change a password or issue reset authorization automatically.

Never disclose an existing password, ask a user to put their recovery key into public chat/GitHub, or approve account takeover from a user-ID-only request. The recovery-key route is the normal email-independent reset mechanism; missing credentials require a controlled identity process.

Advanced temporary-password accounts

Use Advanced · manually provision a temporary-password account only when ordinary self-signup is unsuitable. Choose a regular-user ID and optional professional role, link the intended legacy request where applicable, and select Generate account & temporary password.

Copy the unique temporary credentials when shown, share them only through an appropriate private channel with the intended user, and dismiss the secret. The app does not email it automatically or provide a reusable shared default password. It expires, is not retrievable later, and the user must set a permanent password before receiving normal app access. Reissue only for the intended pending account; earlier temporary credentials stop working.

Account messaging is not public chat

Private approval/status messages are separate from Ask PV Info's public-update search. Current chat should not be advertised as a live support channel or a guaranteed administrator inbox. Keep messages organizational and minimal; do not collect names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers or patient information.

chapters.summary: Maintain collection connectors, discover official documents and review public editorial changes.
chapters.html:
Maintain collection connectors, discover official documents and review public editorial changes.

Data sources: configure collection

Open Data sources. The registry is the configured collection list, not a promise that every public source is reachable. Search/filter to find an existing source before adding a duplicate.

  1. Choose the appropriate type: RSS/Atom, JSON API, web page or news search.
  2. Enter a stable source ID, organizational name/classification, URL and supported region/topic/parser settings.
  3. Use supported credential placeholders and the private credential controls if needed. Do not paste credential values into a public source URL, public notes or a GitHub issue.
  4. Save, then use Test now to inspect the immediate result. A successful test does not guarantee every later run will succeed.
  5. Activate, pause/deactivate or resume collection with the requested organizational reason. When offered, choose a catch-up window appropriate to the source.
  6. After the next data publication, check actual collection results and public coverage.

Deactivation is different from a temporary upstream error. A failed source should not silently disappear from configuration or erase prior successful evidence. Use the supported history/revert controls carefully: inspect the earlier configuration and record why it is being restored. HTTP status, parser format, counts and last-success context help distinguish a feed problem from a publication problem.

Source Discovery: find candidate documents

Open Source Discovery. Publication connectors monitor approved official indexes, RSS/Atom or a supported sitemap list. They produce candidate documents for review; they do not recursively crawl all history or automatically approve legal requirements.

Use Add publication connector to configure the verified agency, official URL, keywords/scope and available schedule controls. Review Publication connectors and Recent discovery checks, or Scan now for an authorized immediate request. Filter Discovery inbox by agency and candidate status: Awaiting review, Deferred, Registered or Rejected.

Open a candidate's official publication, confirm document identity/type/scope, then use the offered registration/review controls. Register the intended document family in Source Documents rather than creating multiple families for the same evolving document. A rejected/deferred candidate retains its disposition; it is not a public approved requirement. Failed or duplicate candidates must not silently create new baselines.

Source and requirement editorial workflows

Use Source Documents for capture configuration/agency verification, Baseline Review for automatic drafts, Requirements Library for versioned interpretations/releases and Regulatory Change Review for human source-change triage. Source registration, capture, draft creation, triage and approval are distinct operations.

Public resource and research reviews

Use Safety resources for directory entries and feedback. Use Research review for tags, maturity/relevance, summary review and paper-version relationships. Keep company-confidential applicability decisions in private assessments, not public editorial annotations.

Company directory and approvals

The main Admin screen exposes company-list approval and supported company overrides/additions. Review the manifest/coverage information, use the offered organizational approval rationale and inspect the resulting public profile after data publication. Hiding or editing a public directory company is not the same as deleting private user cases or erasing a company's historical source evidence.

Activity and responsible editing

Inspect available admin activity/history after important changes. A successful save records configuration, but public snapshots may not update until publication. If an edit conflicts with another user's revision, reload and compare before retrying. Do not bypass source-host, access, version or approval checks to make a record appear complete.

chapters.summary: Operate data refresh independently of app releases, inspect failures and manage menus.
chapters.html:
Operate data refresh independently of app releases, inspect failures and manage menus.

Open Data Refresh Center

From Admin choose Open refresh controls, or open Data Refresh Center. It shows Updates & research, Products & markets and Clinical portfolios, with scheduler check/attempt/success/next-due information and recent run outcomes. Reload status requests current state.

Set a frequency or request a run

  1. Choose a supported Refresh frequency for a pipeline and Save schedule. Updates defaults to twice daily (every 12 hours) and also supports hourly; other supported choices include daily/weekly and Paused as offered.
  2. Use Queue refresh to request fresh work at the next scheduler check.
  3. For unfinished clinical work, Resume unfinished requests continuation where supported.
  4. Use Open GitHub workflow when a maintainer needs to run the workflow immediately with Force. A public app administrator is not automatically authorized to manage the GitHub repository.
  5. Read collection outcome and publication state separately.

The updates scheduler checks hourly at minute 23; it collects only when the saved interval is due or work is queued. Other pipelines keep their own checks. GitHub can delay runs. The twice-daily setting is an interval target, not a guaranteed fixed clock time. Pausing stops scheduled eligibility and clears queued work; it does not cancel an already active run. An authorized forced manual run can still execute when paused. Schedule edits use revision checks; a conflict requires reload before saving again.

Interpret run states

State or indicatorMeaning
QueuedWork was requested but has not necessarily started.
RunningAn active leased run is collecting/publishing. A missing heartbeat needs investigation.
SuccessThe reported collection completed successfully according to that pipeline's checks.
PartialSome source/company work is incomplete; read failure counts and last-success evidence.
Failed/interruptedThe run did not complete normally. Earlier published data should remain available under its existing freshness rules.
