chapters.title: Synthetic Safety Sandbox
chapters.summary: Create fictional scenarios, compare structured rules and inspect demonstration deadlines in a temporary local workspace.
chapters.html:
Use this training workspace to construct fictional clinical or marketed case scenarios and compare reporting-rule assumptions. It is not a production safety database or a complete implementation of ICH E2B(R3).

Read the full use, validation and trademark notice. The tools and exports are independent training artifacts, not regulatory submissions or evidence of vendor endorsement. Choosing a local CIOMS template does not grant rights in that form.

Open and start

Open Resources → Synthetic Safety Sandbox from the Resources page, or follow the Configuration Workbench link. Start with Cases, Scenario Library or Rule Lab. Choose New case for a blank record, or start a fictional scenario from the library. Everything stays in page memory. Closing or reloading clears the working session; downloaded files remain on your device. No case records are transmitted or saved in browser storage.

Use fictional information only. The form intentionally has no patient/reporter names, date of birth, email, phone or address fields. Short text labels are not an anonymization service: do not paste real case information into them.

Your case workspace

The Cases dashboard shows saved revisions as cards. Search by case ID, medicine, event or country; filter by lifecycle, structural review status or earlier revisions. Summary cards distinguish structural issues from the requirements needed to run XML checks. Ready to test means the demonstration rules can run; it does not mean clinical completeness or XML validation has passed.

Open a case to work through Intake → Patient → Products → Events → Assessment → Narrative → Review → Export. Previous/Continue buttons and the step navigation keep the same draft. Returning to Cases or Scenario Library keeps unsaved edits in this tab; choose Resume draft to continue. Opening a different case or scenario asks before discarding edits. Reloading or closing the tab still clears the entire session.

Review brings structural issues, XML profile requirements, changes since the saved revision and the last saved revision’s changes together. Repeated rows are compared by their stable IDs. Save a new revision with its type and reason before testing saved cases or downloading the saved-case package.

The Scenario Library includes a clinical reporting clock, multiple products/events, gestation zero, conflicting null flavor, follow-up without clock reset and missing initial receipt. Each creates a separate fictional case. Sample dates, assessments and clocks are editable training assumptions.

Case form

  1. Case and receipt: synthetic ID, country, clinical/marketed scope, source, reporter qualification, initial receipt, latest information, simulated submission and explicit case-level seriousness, unexpectedness and relatedness.
  2. Patient and study: fictional age/unit, sex, weight, height, pregnancy, gestation, study reference, phase and study type. Zero and unknown are distinct.
  3. Products: up to 20 independent products with stable row IDs, ingredient, role, strength, form, dose, route, indication, treatment dates, action, dechallenge and rechallenge. Each product also supports up to 20 dose regimens with amount/unit, frequency, route, dates, duration and fictional batch reference. These are training labels, not dictionary-coded medicines.
  4. Events: up to 20 events with stable IDs, terms, onset/end, outcome, seriousness criteria and explicit term-availability choices. No MedDRA terminology is distributed.
  5. Assessment matrix: causality, expectedness and a reference basis for every product–event pair. Opposite assessments for different pairs are preserved. Removing a product or event removes its associated pairs from the current draft only.
  6. Tests and history: repeatable structured tests/results/units and medical history with dates and ongoing status, up to 20 rows each.
  7. Literature and linked reports: up to 20 fictional citations with reference/DOI and language; linked case reference and amendment context.
  8. Parent–child and death: fictional parent demographics/history, death date/cause and autopsy context. No identity fields.
  9. Narrative and exchange context: fictional clinical narrative and reporter/sender comments, worldwide case reference, sender/receiver identifiers, reporter country and study sponsor/protocol. No gateway connection is created.
  10. Revisions: save the initial case, then record a reason and choose follow-up, correction or restore. Each save creates a new revision and preserves the previous snapshot. Case ID is locked after first save. A known initial receipt is locked; a previously missing receipt can be completed in a reasoned new revision, preserving the earlier blank snapshot. Up to 100 earlier snapshots are supported. Restore creates a draft from an earlier snapshot; saving makes another revision. Latest-information time does not move backwards.
  11. Preview and export: check structural issues, preview the case report and download the original PV Info training PDF. PDF reflects the current form, including unsaved changes, and is labeled draft. Save first to capture a complete revision record.

The form covers the sections listed here. It does not implement every ICH/regional ICSR element, full parent drug/history repeatability, linked attachments, sender/receiver XML envelopes or licensed terminology validation. Fictional narratives are limited to 4,000 characters each; citation and parent/autopsy text are limited to 1,000 characters each.

Rule simulation

Save cases before running. The current and proposed rules use explicit case-level country, scope, seriousness, unexpectedness and relatedness; all selected conditions must match. The pair matrix is retained as evidence and is not automatically combined into a medical judgment. Unknown yields an indeterminate result unless a different condition definitively excludes the case.

Times are UTC. Deadline = selected receipt timestamp + configured days × 24 hours. Initial receipt is the default. Choosing latest-information time requires an explicit rationale and is only a simulation assumption; a follow-up does not automatically reset the clock. Business-day, regional clock and vendor auto-scheduling policies are not implemented. Missing receipt, contradictory event seriousness, invalid chronology, conflicting null flavors or an incomplete pair matrix block simulation and explain why.

Results distinguish not triggered, indeterminate, blocked and triggered; triggered results show pending/overdue or met/missed against the simulated submission time. They explain each condition and preserve inputs in a downloadable results package.

Save, import and restore

Use Import, download & session controls to download saved cases, restore files or close the session. Draft edits are not included in saved-case packages. Closing clears cases, drafts, rules, results and the locally selected CIOMS template.

  • Saved case package (JSON): preserves saved cases, repeatable sections and revision history. Restore accepts the versioned synthetic format, checks IDs/history and replaces the current case collection after confirmation. Maximum 200 cases and 2 MB per imported package. Download this before closing.
  • Legacy CSV: fixed columns only, up to 200 cases / 200 KB. It creates simple single-product/single-event cases. CSV cannot carry repeatable sections or revision history. Use JSON to preserve richer cases.
  • Reproducible test package: records engine version, rules, saved cases, simulation time, clock assumptions and outcomes. This results file is evidence of a training run; restore uses the separate saved-case package.

Local revisions are not a tamper-proof audit trail and have no authenticated reviewer attribution. Imported files are not evidence of regulatory approval.

PDF and XML exports

PDF print creates a PV Info synthetic training report. It is not a CIOMS form or an official regulator report. Review the fictional form before export.

CIOMS template filling and coded case XML download are disabled pending documented rights review. MedDRA code-entry controls are unavailable. PV Info has no licensed dictionary subscription and does not provide dictionary coding, synonym expansion or membership validation. Generic source-code schema tooling and structural mapping reports do not grant terminology or form rights.

Use fictional data only. Ordinary package export is for local training review; do not import or redistribute restricted terminology or third-party form content.

Ready to test means the demonstration rules can run; it does not mean clinical completeness or XML validation has passed.

Open a case to work through Intake → Patient → Products → Events → Assessment → Narrative → Review → Export. Previous/Continue buttons and the step navigation keep the same draft. Returning to Cases or Scenario Library keeps unsaved edits in this tab; choose Resume draft to continue. Opening a different case or scenario asks before discarding edits. Reloading or closing the tab still clears the entire session.

Review brings structural issues, XML profile requirements, changes since the saved revision and the last saved revision’s changes together. Repeated rows are compared by their stable IDs. Save a new revision with its type and reason before testing saved cases or downloading the saved-case package.

The Scenario Library includes a clinical reporting clock, multiple products/events, gestation zero, conflicting null flavor, follow-up without clock reset and missing initial receipt. Each creates a separate fictional case. Sample dates, assessments and clocks are editable training assumptions.

 Case form

1. Case and receipt: synthetic ID, country, clinical/marketed scope, source, reporter qualification, initial receipt, latest information, simulated submission and explicit case-level seriousness, unexpectedness and relatedness.
2. Patient and study: fictional age/unit, sex, weight, height, pregnancy, gestation, study reference, phase and study type. Zero and unknown are distinct.
3. Products: up to 20 independent products with stable row IDs, ingredient, role, strength, form, dose, route, indication, treatment dates, action, dechallenge and rechallenge. Each product also supports up to 20 dose regimens with amount/unit, frequency, route, dates, duration and fictional batch reference. These are training labels, not dictionary-coded medicines.
4. Events: up to 20 events with stable IDs, terms, onset/end, outcome, seriousness criteria and explicit term-availability choices. No MedDRA terminology is distributed.
5. Assessment matrix: causality, expectedness and a reference basis for every product–event pair. Opposite assessments for different pairs are preserved. Removing a product or event removes its associated pairs from the current draft only.
6. Tests and history: repeatable structured tests/results/units and medical history with dates and ongoing status, up to 20 rows each.
7. Literature and linked reports: up to 20 fictional citations with reference/DOI and language; linked case reference and amendment context.
8. Parent–child and death: fictional parent demographics/history, death date/cause and autopsy context. No identity fields.
9. Narrative and exchange context: fictional clinical narrative and reporter/sender comments, worldwide case reference, sender/receiver identifiers, reporter country and study sponsor/protocol. No gateway connection is created.
10. Revisions: save the initial case, then record a reason and choose follow-up, correction or restore. Each save creates a new revision and preserves the previous snapshot. Case ID is locked after first save. A known initial receipt is locked; a previously missing receipt can be completed in a reasoned new revision, preserving the earlier blank snapshot. Up to 100 earlier snapshots are supported. Restore creates a draft from an earlier snapshot; saving makes another revision. Latest-information time does not move backwards.
11. Preview and export: check structural issues, preview the case report and download the original PV Info training PDF. PDF reflects the current form, including unsaved changes, and is labeled draft. Save first to capture a complete revision record.

The form covers the sections listed here. It does not implement every ICH/regional ICSR element, full parent drug/history repeatability, linked attachments, sender/receiver XML envelopes or licensed terminology validation. Fictional narratives are limited to 4,000 characters each; citation and parent/autopsy text are limited to 1,000 characters each.

 Rule simulation

Save cases before running. The current and proposed rules use explicit case-level country, scope, seriousness, unexpectedness and relatedness; all selected conditions must match. The pair matrix is retained as evidence and is not automatically combined into a medical judgment. Unknown yields an indeterminate result unless a different condition definitively excludes the case.

Times are UTC. Deadline = selected receipt timestamp + configured days × 24 hours. Initial receipt is the default. Choosing latest-information time requires an explicit rationale and is only a simulation assumption; a follow-up does not automatically reset the clock. Business-day, regional clock and vendor auto-scheduling policies are not implemented. Missing receipt, contradictory event seriousness, invalid chronology, conflicting null flavors or an incomplete pair matrix block simulation and explain why.

Results distinguish not triggered, indeterminate, blocked and triggered; triggered results show pending/overdue or met/missed against the simulated submission time. They explain each condition and preserve inputs in a downloadable results package.

 Save, import and restore

Use Import, download & session controls to download saved cases, restore files or close the session. Draft edits are not included in saved-case packages. Closing clears cases, drafts, rules, results and the locally selected CIOMS template.

- Saved case package (JSON): preserves saved cases, repeatable sections and revision history. Restore accepts the versioned synthetic format, checks IDs/history and replaces the current case collection after confirmation. Maximum 200 cases and 2 MB per imported package. Download this before closing.
- Legacy CSV: fixed columns only, up to 200 cases / 200 KB. It creates simple single-product/single-event cases. CSV cannot carry repeatable sections or revision history. Use JSON to preserve richer cases.
- Reproducible test package: records engine version, rules, saved cases, simulation time, clock assumptions and outcomes. This results file is evidence of a training run; restore uses the separate saved-case package.

Local revisions are not a tamper-proof audit trail and have no authenticated reviewer attribution. Imported files are not evidence of regulatory approval.

 PDF and XML exports

PDF print creates a PV Info synthetic training report. It is not a CIOMS form or an official regulator report. Review the fictional form before export.

CIOMS template filling and coded case XML download are disabled pending documented rights review. MedDRA code-entry controls are unavailable. PV Info has no licensed dictionary subscription and does not provide dictionary coding, synonym expansion or membership validation. Generic source-code schema tooling and structural mapping reports do not grant terminology or form rights.

Use fictional data only. Ordinary package export is for local training review; do not import or redistribute restricted terminology or third-party form content.

chapters.title: US Approval & Label Journey
chapters.summary: Trace FDA original decisions, supplements, official documents and available DailyMed label versions; compare source wording with explicit date and identity boundaries.
chapters.html:
Find an FDA application

Open Label Intelligence → US Approval & Label Journey, or follow the journey link from Label Intelligence, Product Evidence Answers or a US application answer in Ask PV Info. This public lookup does not require a company portfolio.

Search by brand, active ingredient or FDA application. Suggestions appear as you type at least three characters; the Search button also works with two. Choose the matching FDA application explicitly. Spaced and lowercase identifiers such as NDA 020702 are normalized. Generic products and multiple applications remain separate choices; a matching name is not proof of presentation equivalence.

The summary reads live openFDA Drugs@FDA records. It distinguishes the earliest captured approved original submission from the source sponsor and the products currently listed under the application. A later presentation's own first approval, historical original applicant, first worldwide approval and ingredient-first approval are not established by that application date.

Read the approval and document evidence

Select a presentation to inspect its ingredient strengths, dosage form, administration route and source status. The regulatory application type (NDA, ANDA or BLA) is separate from administration route. Sponsor means the name reported in the current source snapshot, not a verified original applicant or current commercial owner.

Original-decision evidence shows only documents listed by FDA. A Review remains a Review; the app does not invent an approval-letter link when none is returned. Document dates can be later than the approval decision. The underlying FDA JSON, application page, record hash, source update and retrieval time remain available.

Follow decisions and versions together

The timeline includes original submissions, supplements and other submission statuses. Approved submissions use the source approval-decision date; non-approved statuses are not called approvals. Each record exposes the supplied classification, review priority and available label, letter and review links.

Label-linked decisions + SPL selects submissions with a listed label document or source labeling classification, plus submitted SPL versions. This does not establish that each supplement concerns a specific safety term or that each SPL version corresponds to a listed supplement.

Choose a DailyMed label family using the labeler and Set ID. FDA application links can span multiple labels, formulations and presentations. No dates are automatically joined to declare a supplement and an SPL version equivalent.

Load additional history pages with More history entries. Retrieve individual versions from the timeline. Every retrieved version must report the selected Set ID and FDA application. A version with missing or different application metadata is blocked in this combined journey; inspect it separately in the standalone Label History tool. Retrieval is bounded to 50 versions and 6 MB of text per session.

Filter and compare wording

Use date range, source-record type, SPL date basis, section and phrase filters. DailyMed publication date is available from its history index. An SPL effective date is shown only after retrieving its XML. Filtering by effective date excludes versions whose effective date has not been retrieved. Invalid date ranges show a correction prompt.

Section and phrase filters search retrieved narrative text only and exclude FDA decisions and unretrieved versions. Missing results do not establish absence of a warning or adverse reaction. This is a literal text search, not a licensed MedDRA or SMQ expansion.

Retrieve two versions of the same family, select an earlier and later version, and choose Compare wording. Red marks removed words/punctuation; green marks additions. The comparison preserves the extracted source text, including whitespace. Large changed ranges use an explicitly labeled bounded fallback. Images, original document layout and scientific interpretation are not compared. The comparison follows its chosen version pair and section filter; timeline date and phrase filters do not change that pair.

A text difference does not explain a regulatory reason. The app displays the source submission classification, but a reason for a particular wording change requires review of the original letter, assessment and label. First observed mention remains distinct from confirmed first approved addition.

Export and coverage

Download the journey evidence as JSON. It includes application and product metadata, submission decisions and official document links, the selected presentation and family, loaded history index, retrieved version text and hashes, failed retrievals, comparison and active filters. Keep the export with its source dates and limitations.

The newest retrieved SPL is not labeled as the verified current approved label. Historical coverage, particularly before 2009 and between listed versions, can be incomplete. Official document links are supplied as listed by FDA; the app does not attest to their reachability, contents or regulatory applicability. Original-applicant identities and term-specific approved first additions are not inferred. Qualified human review is mandatory.

chapters.title: Country Explorer
chapters.summary: Explore available country product records, source company roles and safety evidence with explicit coverage.
chapters.html:
Select a jurisdiction

Open Explore → Country Explorer. Use Find a country to narrow the selector by country name, code or configured search terms, then select Explore. The current product repository supports US, Canadian and EU source records. For EU member countries, the product view shows EU centrally evaluated evidence; it does not establish national availability. Other countries retain regulator links and available safety updates, with the national registry marked as not connected.

Read products and company roles

Search by product, ingredient, source company name or application identifier. Search ignores case, accepts spaced FDA application identifiers and allows words in different orders. Filter by source category and status group. Counts are source records, with possible overlap between registries; they are not counts of unique marketed medicines.

An NDC listing is not FDA approval. A source authorisation does not establish that a medicine is marketed. Source company roles are not proof of global commercial ownership. Open official evidence links to verify each record. US application records can link into the US Approval & Label Journey.

Review and export evidence

The Companies view groups source company names within the current product filters. Safety updates search captured country updates independently of the product filters. The Clinical activity tab retrieves country-located ClinicalTrials.gov interventional drug and biological studies on demand. Use the same clinical phase overview as Company Portfolio: click a phase tile to filter, or click it again to clear the phase. Counts reflect loaded studies after search and status filters; a study with multiple phases appears in each applicable tile, so counts are not additive. Phase not stated retains studies with missing phase data. Readable status labels and Ongoing studies use the shared company clinical definitions. Filter loaded studies by phase, overall study status and search terms. Load subsequent registry pages explicitly. The source query total includes records excluded from this medicine-only view. Overall status is not local site recruitment status, and study medicines may include comparators and placebo. A country switch clears clinical pages and continuation tokens. Failed requests preserve previously loaded evidence for retry. A missing or unavailable snapshot is a coverage gap, not evidence that no records exist.

Export downloads the filtered loaded product and update records with coverage information and limitations. It contains no live verification of national completeness. Review source dates before using a downloaded file; exports can become stale.

Share a filtered view

The URL preserves the country, view, query, source and status filters plus clinical phase and study status. Clinical data is loaded on demand when reopening a link. Phase tiles show Not loaded until a registry page is received; zero counts then describe loaded evidence only. Company groups retain matches found through product or ingredient search.

chapters.title: Portfolio Label Watch import preview
chapters.summary: Import a portfolio, explicitly confirm source matches and download a private review package.
chapters.html:
Import and review

Open Label Intelligence → Portfolio Label Watch. Upload a CSV containing business product information only, with a market column (US, EU or CA) and a brand, ingredient or identifier. Use the downloadable header template. The NDC column accepts two-part product NDCs only; package-level identifiers are rejected with an explanation instead of silently returning no matches. Matching preserves punctuation and does not infer brand or ingredient synonyms. Maximum size is 200 KB and 500 product rows. The file remains in this tab; the app requests source datasets without uploading your CSV.

Confirm one source record or exclude each row. Supplied fields constrain candidates; nothing is automatically confirmed. If more than 100 records match, narrow the input before confirming. Source company roles do not establish ownership. Availability depends on source coverage and a secure browser context for verified repository retrieval.

Create a private package

Create reviewed portfolio to inspect ingredients, source company roles, source dates and available US journey links. Download the private JSON package to retain selections and provenance. Closing or reloading the tab discards the in-memory work. Restore a downloaded JSON package to load its product identities as an unverified baseline. Current source metadata is compared against saved hash, status and approval-date values. All matches require confirmation again. Missing records do not establish withdrawal, and metadata differences do not establish label wording changes. This preview has no account sync, scheduled monitoring or alerts. A new import replaces the current in-memory preview.

The package includes portfolio selections and should remain private. No reporting deadline, complete label history or first approved safety-term addition is inferred from the matched source record.

Refresh evidence

Refresh source evidence requests published snapshots again and clears prior confirmations. Restoring a package also refreshes evidence. Retrieval time is separate from source publication time; a newly retrieved snapshot can still contain older source records. Confirm matches again before exporting.
